$comment: APPEND ONLY. A code is minted once and never reused, never renumbered, never deleted — a code pasted from a chat log a year old must still resolve to the same failure. To stop using one, set retired:true and leave it in place; errorcodes_test.go fails on a gap in the sequence, which is what makes that rule mechanical rather than remembered.

codes.meaning: Your session has expired, so the platform refused the request.
codes.remedy: Run `drift account login` and try again. Sessions are 12 hours; this is the ordinary way one ends.

codes.meaning: The platform accepted your identity but refused the action.
codes.remedy: The account is authenticated and lacks the permission for this operation. If it is meant to be your own slice, you may be on a different account than you think — `drift slice list` shows what this one actually has.

codes.meaning: The thing you named does not exist on the platform.
codes.remedy: Check the spelling, and that your active slice is the one you mean — `drift slice list` shows what the account actually has.

codes.meaning: You have hit a quota on your plan.
codes.remedy: The message names which one. Free a slot by deleting something you no longer need, or raise the limit on the form `drift slice resize` draws.

codes.meaning: The platform failed while handling the request. This one is ours, not yours.
codes.remedy: Nothing you changed caused it. Retry once; if it persists, the failure is on the platform side and status.ondrift.eu carries the per-component picture.

codes.meaning: The CLI could not reach the Drift API at all.
codes.remedy: No response came back, so this is the network between you and the platform, or the platform being down. Check your connection first, then status.ondrift.eu.

codes.meaning: The request to the platform timed out.
codes.remedy: The platform accepted the connection and did not answer in time. Retry; a deploy that timed out may still have landed, so check with `drift file simulate` before deploying again.

codes.meaning: This machine has no copy of the Driftfile format, so a Driftfile cannot be validated.
codes.remedy: The platform defines the format and the CLI caches it on first contact. Run any online command once — `drift account login` or `drift slice list` — and it is cached permanently at ~/.drift/driftfile.schema.json.
The message names the field and what it expected. `drift file lint` reports every problem at once, offline, which is faster than fixing them one deploy at a time.

codes.meaning: A compiled function booked less memory than its language runtime needs.
codes.remedy: Go and Rust carry a private runtime inside every invocation, so they floor at 16MB where the interpreted languages floor at 8MB. Raise the booking, or run `drift file benchmark` against a deployed slice to size it from what it actually holds.

codes.meaning: You are not logged in, so the CLI has no credential to send.
codes.remedy: Run `drift account login`, or `drift account signup` if you do not have an account yet. This is different from an expired session (DRIFT-1001): there is no session on this machine at all.
